---
title: "B: SFT on teacher outputs"
subtitle: "Sequence-level distillation, and the headline method"
---

{{< include /_setup.qmd >}}

**Question.** If the student simply copies the teacher's answers, how far does it get without a
single label?

**Setup.** The 2B answers all `{python} n(teacher["rows"])` training queries once, greedily, with
thinking off (`{python} f"{teacher['gpu_hours']:.1f}"` GPU-hours). Its answers are parsed and
written back as clean JSON; the `{python} n(teacher["unparsed"])` that don't parse are dropped,
leaving `{python} n(teacher["variants"]["unfiltered"]["kept"])`. Gold is never read: the teacher's
answers agree with it on `{python} pct(teacher["variants"]["unfiltered"]["lenient"])` of them, under
lenient exact. Then the same SFT recipe as A.

::: {.facts}
```{python}
table(["B"])
```
:::

```{ojs}
runs = ["B"]
```

{{< include /_run.qmd >}}

## What it shows

- **The student beats its teacher on xLAM.** `{python} story.score("B")` against
  `{python} story.score("raw 2B")` on test-clean (`{python} story.claim("B", "raw 2B", "test-clean")`),
  and `{python} h["share_of_a"]` of what gold labels gain. It isn't format: most of the 2B's
  answers that fail to parse are a call cut short, not a bracket slip. And it isn't memorisation: no
  test-clean query is in train, and B's lead is larger on rows whose tool set train never saw.
- **On unseen tools, it stays below the teacher, though not after Holm**
  (`{python} story.claim("B", "raw 2B", "bfcl")`): it gets argument values wrong on tools it never
  saw. Its BFCL keeps rising after its selected checkpoint, to
  `{python} pct(last["B"]["bfcl"]["exact"])` at the end of its epoch.
- **It is the headline method.** C, D and grounded B can't be separated from it on test-clean. It is
  the simplest of them, at a cost within 10% of the cheapest (grounded B); that reading of the tie
  rule was chosen after the results were known, and is recorded as such.
